name: S&P 500 Shiller CAPE
derived: Expected US real return over 10 years about 3.6% a year (80% band -1.9% to 9.2%); ECY model R2 0.33 (n=1631 months); EY model R2 0.25 (n=1631 months)

name: Excess CAPE yield (1/CAPE minus real 10-year yield)
reading: 20th percentile since 1881 (low = stocks expensive against bonds)
derived: The equity premium over real bonds that today's price leaves; the lower it is, the less stocks pay for their extra risk

name: S&P 500 total-return CAPE
reading: Corrects CAPE for the shift from dividends to buybacks

name: US yield curve, 10 years minus 3 months
reading: Average of the last 30 days; negative = inverted
derived: Chance of a US recession within 12 months about 16% (NY Fed yield-curve model)
source: US Treasury par yield curve; NY Fed probit (-0.5333, -0.6330)

name: US yield curve, 10 years minus 2 years
reading: Positive after an inversion often comes late in the cycle

name: US 10-year Treasury yield
derived: The discount rate for every asset priced in dollars

name: VIX, expected S&P 500 volatility
derived: Fear above 30 has historically been a better time to buy than to sell; below 13 nobody is paid for risk

name: MOVE, expected Treasury volatility
reading: Bond-market fear; high readings preceded the 2022 rate shock and the 2023 bank failures
derived: Watch with VIX: both high = forced selling

name: High-yield vs Treasury bonds (HYG/IEF, total return)
derived: A fall of 5% or more from the high has marked widening credit spreads; Burry's 2005-07 signal was credit, not stocks

name: S&P 500 against its 200-day average
derived: 12-month change +4.0%; a falling market below its 200-day average is where crashes happen

name: Swiss Performance Index against its 200-day average
derived: 12-month change +17.7%; a falling market below its 200-day average is where crashes happen

name: MSCI World against its 200-day average
derived: 12-month change +5.7%; a falling market below its 200-day average is where crashes happen

name: Euro Stoxx 50 against its 200-day average
derived: 12-month change +6.7%; a falling market below its 200-day average is where crashes happen

name: S&P 500 equal weight against cap weight (RSP/SPY)
reading: +8.2% over 1 year; ratio at the 8th percentile of its history
derived: How much of the market's gain comes from its largest stocks; Burry's 2019 passive-concentration argument

name: US small caps against the S&P 500 (IWM/SPY)
reading: +2.9% over 1 year; ratio at the 5th percentile of its history
derived: Neglected small caps are where Burry looks for value

name: US value against growth (IWD/IWF)
reading: +38.9% over 1 year; ratio at the 24th percentile of its history

name: EUR/CHF
derived: Below 0.90 the SNB tends to lean against the franc; a strong franc cuts the foreign earnings of Swiss multinationals

name: Copper/gold ratio
derived: Falling = markets price weaker growth or more fear; it usually moves with long bond yields
